Can you take a line drawing apart into living layers?

amodal layered decomposition of line art · BLUELINE shot 02 · the steps, and the wall · 2026-06-25

1 · Segment — three ways, all short

Authored boxes (A), SAM-auto (B, over-segments into fragments), SAM-prompted (C). The figure came out best from our keypoint mask, not SAM. And none separated the car. Photo-trained SAM learns that an object is a solid textured region; a line-art car is sparse outline strokes on the same paper, so there is no region to grab and it snaps to the nearest tonal block.

2 · The car defeats the line-structure methods too

Close-the-outline-and-fill (A) and convex hull (C) over-fill the whole box (the ink connects into one blob); GrabCut (B) grabs a rough half; +largest-component (D) is still the whole blob. No clean car boundary exists at the pixel level — the car is only perceptually grouped by a human reading the drawing.

3 · Depth — the surprise win

Depth Anything V2 runs on the drawing and recovers a correct front-to-back order (street/person closest → cars/buildings → smoke/sky farthest). Bonus: a clean person silhouette falls out for free — a second independent route to the figure. Depth retired the whole Ordering skill.

4 · Depth bands — a free coarse decomposition

Threshold the depth into FRONT / MID / BACK and each band is a usable, correctly-ordered cel — person+street, cars+buildings, fire+sky — with zero segmentation. This is how far 'free' auto-decomposition reaches before per-element refinement is needed.

5 · Complete — LaMa reconstructs what the figure hid

Remove the man, and LaMa (Large-Mask Inpainting) rebuilds the car, fire, and street behind him plausibly — not cv2.inpaint's blur (which the eye rejects). It fills texture; exact occluded line-shape is the deeper, still-open part.

6 · Read the physics out of the drawing

A structure-tensor analysis of the drawn smoke measures its flow direction by height — it leans consistently up-and-to-the-right (mean 0.63). The image's own physics, extracted, then used to drive the motion.

7 · Compose — the pen lines come alive

The drawing's own fire/smoke strokes are warped along that measured flow (rise + lick + up-right lean), masked to the plume, the man extracted and his hole infilled with fire, the buildings locked, the man held crisp on top, slow and looped. No overlay — the existing ink moves.

8 · The breakthrough — decompose in PHOTOREAL, stylize last

▸ the predicted breakthrough — the validation render (FLUX canny→photoreal) is queued; the reasoning below stands, the image fills in when it lands.

The insight that dissolves the wall: don't fight line-art. Convert the drawing to photoreal (FLUX + canny ControlNet, same composition) — now SAM and depth lock the car instantly, because in photoreal it is a solid object they were trained on. Segment + infill in the domain where the tools are strong, then re-apply the ink style to each clean cel. Rich-first / stylize-last, applied to layering.

What works, and the wall

elementbest toolextent
person / figureskeypoints or depth silhouette✓ clean (two routes)
sky · buildings · grounddepth bands✓ coarse, ordered
fire / smokeregion + flow analysis + ink-warp✓ animatable
occluded backgroundLaMa infill✓ texture (not exact shape)
depth orderingDepth Anything V2✓
thin line-art object (car)— in line-art✗ the wall
…the same car in photorealSAM + depth✓ (step 8)

Conclusion. Automatic decomposition of line art hits a hard wall at thin, see-through objects — they are invisible to segmentation, depth, colour, and morphology alike. Two things get past it: depth (which hands you ordering, the figure, and coarse bands for free), and the photoreal-first reframe — do the decomposition where the tools are trained, then stylize each cel. The reliable pipeline is generate/convert to photoreal → segment + depth + infill → stylize each cel to ink → warp & recompose.
